mrc_national_2021.title: MRC Statement on Nielsen National Television Viewing Estimates Analysis
mrc_national_2021.author: Media Rating Council
mrc_national_2021.quote: MRC believes that Total Usage of Television (TUT) by Persons 18-49 was understated by approximately 2 to 6 percent for the February 2021 measurement period (the period covered by the analyses).
mrc_national_2021.quote_panel: Nielsen identified approximately 9,400 of its total of about 40,000 TV panel homes in the U.S. as of February 2021 that had triggered alerts within Nielsen's systems that, in pre-pandemic times, would have led the home to be withheld from contributing to Nielsen's estimates until the alerts had been addressed by Nielsen personnel.
mrc_national_2021.quote_priority: Of these 9,400, approximately 2,400 of the homes had triggered alerts that were considered “high priority,” in that the condition that led to the alert was deemed to be highly likely related to an issue that would affect Nielsen's ability to collect complete and accurate viewing data from the home.
mrc_national_2021.quote_simulation: Based on its analyses, and Nielsen's simulation of February 2021 ratings results that excluded those panel homes that were assumed to have been impaired from a data contribution standpoint, it appears that there was a generally consistent pattern of underreporting of viewing vs. the simulated results.
mrc_national_2021.quote_stderr: MRC also notes, and users of the data should keep in mind, that this range of impact, as well as the originally reported ratings themselves, are estimates with standard errors associated with them.
supports: roughly 40,000 US metered TV panel homes
about 9,400 homes carrying alerts in February 2021
the correction was a simulation with standard errors, not a recount
in-person visits to panel homes were severely curtailed, not wholly stopped
the alerts flagged homes for potential metering or other problems, i.e. conditions likely to stop Nielsen collecting complete and accurate viewing data from the home
mrc_national_2021.quote_curtailed: Because of widespread restrictions imposed by governmental entities and others that first arose in early 2020 as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as Nielsen's concern for the welfare of its own personnel and panel household members, Nielsen's ability to conduct in-person visits to recruit and maintain homes for its television measurement panels was severely curtailed.

mrc_suspend_2021.title: MRC Statement on Pending Changes to Accreditation Statuses of Nielsen Television Services
mrc_suspend_2021.author: Media Rating Council
mrc_suspend_2021.quote: “While we are disappointed that the situation has come to this, we believe these are the proper actions for the MRC to take at this time,” said George W. Ivie, Executive Director and CEO of the MRC.
mrc_suspend_2021.quote_actions: To suspend the MRC accreditation of Nielsen's National Television service. To remove the current accreditation hiatus status designation from Nielsen's Local People Meter and Set Meter Markets services, and to suspend accreditation for these markets.
mrc_suspend_2021.quote_notice: In this instance, Nielsen was informed of the possibility of a suspension action on August 12th for the National Television service, and on August 20th for the Local Market services.
mrc_suspend_2021.quote_effective: Changes to Become Effective in Mid-September
supports: 1 September 2021 MRC board vote to suspend national and local TV accreditation
George W. Ivie is MRC Executive Director and CEO
MRC is a non-profit industry association established in 1963
the Board voted on 1 September 2021; the statement is titled 'Pending Changes' and says the changes become effective in mid-September
mrc_suspend_2021.quote_about: The Media Rating Council is a non-profit industry association established in 1963 comprised of leading television, radio, print and digital media companies, as well as advertisers, advertising agencies and trade associations, whose goal is to ensure measurement services that are valid, reliable and effective.

mrc_reinstate_2023.title: MRC Reinstates Accreditation of Nielsen National Television Service
mrc_reinstate_2023.author: Media Rating Council
mrc_reinstate_2023.quote: New York, NY (April 17, 2023): The Media Rating Council (MRC) today announced that its Board of Directors, at the recommendation of the MRC TV Committee, has reinstated the accreditation of Nielsen's National Television Audience Measurement (TAM) service.
mrc_reinstate_2023.quote_local: This reinstatement excludes the Digital in TV Ratings (dTVR) component of the TAM service, and also does not include Nielsen's Local Market Television Service (which remains in an accreditation suspension status)
mrc_reinstate_2023.quote_cause: Accreditation of the Nielsen National TAM service had been suspended by MRC in September 2021 as a result of a series of standards non-compliance issues, some of which directly resulted from process and panel degradation issues and operational pressures arising from the COVID-19 pandemic.
mrc_reinstate_2023.quote_ivie: Nielsen has undertaken strong efforts to correct the issues that led to its loss of MRC accreditation 19 months ago and to restore key aspects of its panel performance.
supports: local market service still suspended at that date
the suspension is dated September 2021 by MRC itself

mrc_vab_2022.title: MRC Statement on VAB's “Behind Billions of Lost TV Impressions” Report (Amended)
mrc_vab_2022.author: Media Rating Council
mrc_vab_2022.quote: In fact, MRC did not position these figures as “adjustment factors,” nor did MRC recommend they be used in that manner; rather the figures MRC published in May 2021 were presented simply as estimates of ratings understatements that MRC believed occurred in the single month of February 2021.
mrc_vab_2022.quote_report: The Media Rating Council (MRC) would like to correct a representation that was made concerning MRC in a report issued today by the Video Advertising Bureau (VAB) titled “Behind Billions of Lost TV Impressions.”
supports: the VAB tried to use MRC's percentages as adjustment factors
MRC publicly refused that use on 26 January 2022

nielsen_merger_2022.title: Nielsen Enters into Agreement to be Acquired by Evergreen- and Brookfield-Led Consortium for $16 Billion (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1)
nielsen_merger_2022.author: Nielsen Holdings plc
nielsen_merger_2022.quote: NEW YORK, March 29, 2022 /PRNewswire/ — Nielsen Holdings plc (NYSE: NLSN) (“Nielsen”) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by a private equity consortium (“Consortium”) led by Evergreen Coast Capital Corporation (“Evergreen”), an affiliate of Elliott Investment Management L.P. (“Elliott”), and Brookfield Business Partners L.P. together with institutional partners (collectively “Brookfield”) for $28 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $16 billion, including the assumption of debt.
supports: Nielsen agreed on 29 March 2022 to go private at $28 a share, about $16 billion including debt

unverified: The Nielsen client letter of May 2021 said to acknowledge an 'understatement of audience estimates' - never opened; MRC's own 10 May 2021 statement is used instead.

The VAB letter of 14 April 2021 from Sean Cunningham to Nielsen CEO David Kenny demanding an immediate third-party audit - reported by trade press only; the letter itself was not opened, so neither name appears in the prose.
The frequently quoted extrapolation that a 1% undercount equals roughly $39 million in advertising dollars - attributed to the VAB in trade press, no primary document opened; excluded.
Any causal link between the MRC suspension and Nielsen's March 2022 take-private. The prose states the sequence only; no source asserts causation.

The exact effective date of the suspension. MRC's own statement says only 'Changes to Become Effective in Mid-September'; trade press reported 20 September 2021, which was not confirmed against an MRC document.
Whether the total dollar value of US TV advertising priced off these ratings is in the 'tens of billions' - no primary figure opened, so no market-size number appears in the prose.

That Nielsen retained no raw event log at all. The prose previously said 'No stored events to re-read'; no source supports a claim about Nielsen's retention generally. What MRC's 10 May 2021 statement does support is narrower and is what the prose now says: the impaired homes' viewing was never collected, so there was nothing to re-read for them.
That the accreditation suspension took effect on 1 September 2021. The Board voted that day; MRC states only that the changes become effective in mid-September, so the prose says 'voted to suspend'.
